clue.text: Tom left Ginny dancing in place of sailing

indicators.note: the letters are set dancing, moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Tom abandons his partner Ginny on the dance floor and heads off to go sailing instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges TOM, L and GINNY. LYMINGTON is a Hampshire town on England's south coast, famous for its yachting marinas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hampshire harbour town is a well-known yachting centre, hence a place where people go sailing.

clue.text: Fiddle in general brings fictional detective

indicators.note: the fiddle sits in the general, so the first word goes inside the second

parts.note: Robert E. Lee, the American Confederate general
a Strad is a Stradivarius violin, the finest kind of fiddle

explanation.surface: A swindle inside the army brings a detective from a novel onto the case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like a swindle, but it is the violin. Inspector LESTRADE is the Scotland Yard man in the Sherlock Holmes stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Lestrade is the Scotland Yard policeman in Conan Doyle's Sherlock Holmes stories, a character from fiction.

clue.text: Toast to singer?

definitions.meaning: ... toast, thin crisp slices of toasted bread
Dame Nellie ..., the Australian soprano after whom the toast was named

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests raising a glass to a singer; in fact the toast is food named after one.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin crisp toast was named after the famous Australian soprano, so the one name covers both senses.

clue.text: Game with no net's joined to dance

parts.note: a baseball side has nine men and plays without a net, so a team that needs no net belongs to nine men
the morris is a traditional English folk dance performed with bells and sticks

explanation.surface: Some pastime with no netting gets combined with a spot of folk dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Nine men's morris is an old board game for two players. Morris dancing is a traditional English folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine men's morris is an ancient board game for two players, each moving nine pieces, so it is a type of game.

clue.text: The "Crest" to go faster than 1 nm per hour?

parts.note: to top a speed is to exceed or go beyond it
a knot is a speed of one nautical mile per hour

explanation.surface: A ship's figurehead, maybe, invited to exceed a certain speed at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: A knot is one nautical mile (nm) per hour, the unit of speed at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is a tuft of hair or feathers on top of the head, a crest in that sense.

clue.text: Country turning up trumps about liquor

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the whole run of pieces from bottom to top

parts.note: to turn up trumps is to come out excellent, A1, written AI
re means about, concerning
gin is a strong spirit, a liquor

explanation.surface: A nation whose luck proves good on the matter of strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses AI + RE + GIN, giving NIGERIA. 'Trumps' gives AI: to turn up trumps is to prove first-rate, A1.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigeria is a West African nation, a straightforward example of a country.

clue.text: Topping garment, maybe not male, for team mistress

indicators.note: topping a word is cutting off its head, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: a habit, the robe of a nun, a garment perhaps not worn by a man
playing for a team is being on the side

explanation.surface: A garment worn on top, probably by a woman, chosen for the team's female boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' beheads HABIT to leave ABIT. 'Topping garment' reads as a top worn over others, but topping means cutting off the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit on the side is an idiom for a lover kept secretly alongside a spouse, a mistress.

clue.text: Support effective powers to limit of being fed up

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a law with teeth has effective powers to enforce it

explanation.surface: Supporting strong powers right up to the limit of one's patience.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is being 'fed up to the back teeth', utterly sick of something.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom 'fed up to the back teeth', the back teeth mark the furthest point of exasperation.

clue.text: Island once called beautiful thanks one with little colour

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
I is the Roman numeral for one
wan means pale, lacking colour

explanation.surface: A grateful pale individual visits an island with a lovely old name.
explanation.walkthrough: Portuguese sailors named Taiwan Ilha Formosa, 'beautiful island'.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiwan was long known in the West as Formosa, Portuguese for beautiful, so it is the island once called that.

clue.text: What may slip onto some ribs, carrying a threat — it isn't fair

parts.note: a spinal disc can slip, as in a slipped disc

indicators.note: only some of the word ribs is used, its final pair dropped

parts.note: minatory means threatening, carrying a threat

explanation.surface: Something that might slip onto the ribs, with menace, and it is unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' trims RIBS to RI. A slipped disc is a back injury, which suits the talk of ribs.
explanation.definitionFit: Discriminatory treatment is biased and unjust, so it is unfair, which is what the clue's last words say.

clue.text: Social gathering mentioned in I Thessalonians

indicators.note: the answer lies within the letters of the book's name

explanation.surface: A gathering is referred to in one of St Paul's letters in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is inside 'Thessalonians': THES-SALON-IANS.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is a regular gathering of writers, artists and thinkers in a fashionable host's home.

clue.text: Copies single after critic Camille, the opera

indicators.note: the copies and the single come after the critic in the answer

parts.note: Camille Paglia, the American cultural critic
cc stands for carbon copies
I, the Roman numeral one, means single

explanation.surface: Copies of a single record follow a critic's review of an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: PAGLIACCI is Leoncavallo's opera about travelling clowns.
explanation.definitionFit: Pagliacci is Leoncavallo's well-known Italian work for the stage, about a troupe of clowns.

clue.text: Commercial in Latin that works in a way

indicators.note: the commercial is placed in the Latin word, inside its letters

parts.note: a Roman is a Latin, a person of ancient Rome
an ad is a commercial or advertisement

explanation.surface: An advert written in Latin about someone who works in a particular way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' means on a road: a roadman works on road repair.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadman is a worker who repairs roads, so someone whose work is on a way.

clue.text: Educated girl housekeeper gets cheese

indicators.note: the girl gets the house, holding it inside her name

parts.note: Rita of the play and film Educating Rita
read as house-keeper: cot, a small house or cottage, is the house that Rita keeps

explanation.surface: A schooled young woman's housekeeper gets some cheese in.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is Willy Russell's play about a hairdresser studying literature. COT is an old word for a small cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft white Italian whey cheese.

clue.text: Fiend at entering struggle, that is

parts.note: a demon is a fiend

indicators.note: at goes into the word for struggle

parts.note: to strive is to struggle

explanation.surface: A devil arriving to put up a fight, in other words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts the two letters inside the struggle word. 'that is' looks like a link phrase but is the definition: the word 'that' is itself a demonstrative.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'that' is a demonstrative pronoun or adjective, so the clue's last words describe the word itself.

clue.text: Unable to explain setter's corpse — detail that's died

parts.note: my is the setter's way of saying of me

indicators.note: de-tail: the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a stiff is slang for a corpse
ie, id est, means that is
d is short for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: The compiler cannot account for a body: the fine point is that it has expired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detail' looks like a fine point, but read as de-tail it removes the last F of STIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mystified is baffled, unable to account for or understand what is happening.

clue.text: Greek character including those of Crete and so forth

indicators.note: the Greek letter takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: only the letters of the island's name are used, in a new order

explanation.surface: A Greek who takes in some Cretans, and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'those of' reorders the island's letters, and 'including' sets them between the second and third letters of the Greek character.
explanation.definitionFit: Et cetera is Latin for 'and the rest', used to mean and so on.

clue.text: French wine waiter put me right off boy with books and film

indicators.note: the me and the right are taken off the wine waiter

parts.note: a sommelier is a wine waiter, the word being French
taken as written, its two letters removed
Keith, a boy's name
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A French sommelier tells a lad with books to stop bothering him, then sees a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes M, E and R from SOMMELIER, leaving SOMELI. SOME LIKE IT HOT is the 1959 Billy Wilder comedy with Marilyn Monroe.
explanation.definitionFit: Some Like It Hot is Billy Wilder's 1959 comedy starring Marilyn Monroe, Jack Lemmon and Tony Curtis.

clue.text: Yearn for a dance, a simple ball?

parts.note: to long for is to yearn
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Longing for a dance, a modest ball perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a long hop is a short-pitched ball, easy to hit. 'Ball' looks like a dance, but it is a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A long hop is a short, easy delivery in cricket, a simple ball for the batsman to hit.

clue.text: Knighthood for poor Lester can stay in the air

definitions.note: a verb phrase describing the noun: the bird that can hover

parts.note: K stands for a knighthood, as in KBE

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters are in a bad way, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: A knighthood is granted to a hard-up man named Lester who can hover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges LESTER to ESTREL. The definition describes the bird: the kestrel is famous for hovering.
explanation.definitionFit: The kestrel is the small falcon known for hovering, holding still in the air while hunting.

clue.text: Political philosopher's book going for nothing among tramps

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: the book replaces the nothing, going in for it

parts.note: hoboes are tramps
O, the round figure, is nothing

explanation.surface: A political thinker's work turns out worthless among homeless wanderers.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas HOBBES wrote Leviathan.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hobbes, author of Leviathan, is the great English political thinker of the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Greek character, humorist, not starting and not returning

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a comic is a humorist

indicators.note: the word is read back to front

parts.note: nor means and not

explanation.surface: A Greek comedian who has not begun and is not coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' drops C from COMIC; 'returning' turns NOR into RON.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is the fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, its short o.

clue.text: Look noisily for beer and coastal food plant

indicators.note: said out loud, the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to look for is to seek
ale is beer

explanation.surface: Searching loudly for a pint, and finding an edible seaside plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noisily' signals sound: SEEK said aloud is spelt SEAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea kale is a cabbage-family plant of European shorelines, grown for its edible shoots.

clue.text: Some amazement at the villa?

indicators.note: only some of the word is used, the opening part

parts.note: astonishment is amazement

explanation.surface: A hint of wonder at the country house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' trims ASTONISHMENT to its first five letters. Aston Villa is a Birmingham football club, so ASTON is the word that goes before 'villa'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aston Villa is the Birmingham football club, so the district name pairs with the word villa.

clue.text: One of us (identifying him) — I'm commenting on the cold outside

indicators.note: the shivering sound goes round the identification

parts.note: brr is the sound of someone shivering, remarking on the chill
it is he, the formal way of identifying a man

explanation.surface: A Briton is identified as he complains about the chilly weather outside.
explanation.walkthrough: BRR (the shivering noise) goes round IT IS HE. 'One of us' works because the setter writes for a British paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A Britisher is a British person, one of 'us' from the setter's point of view in a British paper.

clue.text: See 6
See 6
Vote for return of an old negative is painfully optimistic

parts.note: to poll is to cast a vote

indicators.note: the next pieces are read backwards

parts.note: nay is the old word for no

explanation.surface: Backing the comeback of an old refusal is far too hopeful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns AN + NAY into YANNA. Pollyanna is the relentlessly cheerful heroine of Eleanor Porter's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollyanna, from Eleanor Porter's novel, means someone excessively, irritatingly cheerful and hopeful.
